log.why: Run E5 on Ticket 1 because {recA, rpoB} has posterior 0.478, giving the most balanced split and highest information gain.
Treating Ticket 2 at 10 µM splits posterior mass closest to 50/50 (0.380 vs 0.620) while Ticket 1 incubates.
Testing hisG directly splits the posterior near 50/50 and pushes hisG above 0.90 if positive.
Ticket 2 has 0.384 mass at or below 3 uM; testing 3 uM cleanly separates the 0.462 peak at 10 uM from lower doses.
10 µM has 0.702 posterior; E4 best splits <=10 µM (0.767) from >10 µM (0.233) while incubators are free.
E7 splits Ticket 3 near 50/50 (0.478 vs 0.522), maximizing information gain while letting it incubate in parallel.
Ticket 2 is tight on time and uncertain; E5 (30 uM) splits its posterior near 58% vs 42% while filling an idle incubator.
hisG has 0.910 posterior after E3 and E5, so publishing now captures a high score before the 23 s deadline.
E4 cleanly separates the leading hypotheses 10 uM (0.388) and 30 uM (0.503) before Ticket 2 expires.
Ticket 2 has 9 s left while E4 needs 6 s, so publishing 30 uM at 0.503 beats certain expiration.
Ticket 3 expires in 9 s, and publishing recA at 0.517 posterior beats the expiration penalty in expected value.
Ticket 4 expires in 30 s; knocking out {sodA, gyrA} splits 0.491 of posterior probability.
E11 splits {sodA, gyrA} from growing E8 and halves the remaining prior mass (0.499 vs 0.501) before Ticket 4 expires.
Ticket 4 expires in 5 s and araC leads at 0.600 posterior, so publishing now avoids expiration and yields positive expected score.
Ticket 7 has the strongest prior lead (araC at 0.410) with 24 s left; testing araC yields 0.887 confidence if positive.
With 17 s left, running E0 on Ticket 7 while E4 incubates tests metJ in parallel before the final publish.
